readme.arch_body.connected: The project has a **connected** architecture: the {shell} shell owns the project root and embeds the web frontend in a native window. The frontend is **not** a standalone website — it is rendered inside the shell.
readme.arch_body.connected_backend: Backend companions live in `backend/` and are reached from the shell over HTTP.
readme.arch_body.separated: The project has a **separated** architecture: `backend/` and `frontend/` are two independent applications in one repository. They talk to each other over HTTP (or through a local dev proxy). Neither side is embedded in the other — each can be developed, tested and deployed on its own.
readme.arch_body.shell_client_api: The project has a **shell + api** architecture: a desktop/mobile client shell (Electron, Expo, React Native, Plasmo) lives in `frontend/` and talks to a REST API backend in `backend/` over HTTP. The client is a standalone application — the backend serves only API traffic and does not render pages.
readme.arch_body.backend_only: The project is **backend-only**: everything lives in the project root, and there is no separate frontend application. All user interaction happens through the API (or CLI) this project exposes.
readme.arch_body.frontend_only: The project is **frontend-only**: there is no separate server-side backend in this project. Code lives in the project root (and in `frontend/` for scaffolded frameworks).
readme.arch_body.frontend_only_fullstack: The selected frontend framework ships its own server, so it can serve both the UI and the API from the same process — but it is not a separate backend application.
readme.arch_body.other: The stack is not classified yet — add at least one language or framework and regenerate the project to get precise instructions.

readme.section.decisions.title: Architectural Decisions
readme.decisions.intro: This section documents important architectural choices made in this project's technology stack:
readme.decisions.reason_multiple: This project uses multiple tools that provide {responsibility} functionality.
readme.decisions.recommendation_multiple: Ensure clear separation of concerns. Document which tool handles which use case.
readme.decision.django_sqlalchemy.reason: Django includes its own ORM — adding SQLAlchemy creates two ORMs in one project.
readme.decision.django_sqlalchemy.recomm: Use the Django ORM in Django projects. Add SQLAlchemy only when you need advanced SQL features or must reuse an existing SQLAlchemy-based data layer.
readme.decision.django_alembic.reason: Django has built-in migrations, while Alembic is a migration tool designed for SQLAlchemy projects.
readme.decision.django_alembic.recommend: Use Django's own migrations (`manage.py makemigrations` / `manage.py migrate`). Alembic only makes sense together with SQLAlchemy.
readme.decision.django_prisma.reason: Prisma is primarily designed for Node.js/TypeScript projects — its Python support is limited.
readme.decision.django_prisma.recommenda: For Python projects use the Django ORM or SQLAlchemy.
readme.decision.fastapi_prisma.reason: Prisma's Python client is at an early pre-release stage — production readiness is limited.
readme.decision.fastapi_prisma.recommend: Consider SQLAlchemy for production Python projects.

readme.mistakes.wrong_dir: Running commands from the wrong directory — run them from the project root (or the exact folder named in the command, e.g. `frontend/`).
readme.mistakes.infra_order: Starting the app before the infrastructure: run `{cmd}` first, otherwise the app fails to connect.
readme.mistakes.local_services: Forgetting that locally installed services must be started manually before the app — see LOCAL_INFRA.md for the exact commands.
readme.mistakes.system_python: Using the system `python` instead of the project venv (`{venv} -m pip ...`) — packages would land in the wrong environment.
readme.mistakes.npm_dir: Running `npm install` in the root when the package.json lives in `frontend/` (or vice versa) — check the Directory map above.
readme.mistakes.embedded: Treating the embedded frontend as a standalone website — it is built into the desktop shell and served from it.
